subject.title: [Bug]: /context detail shows ~62k untracked provider/runtime overhead on fresh OpenAI Codex gpt-5.5 session

question: What token-bucket semantics should `/context detail` use for OpenAI Codex sessions, and which buckets should drive context warnings or compaction decisions?
rationale: Current code can display the gap, and Codex exposes separate usage buckets, but mapping cached/native/provider state into user-facing context, billing, and compaction semantics is a product decision rather than a safe mechanical repair.

options.title: Define the ledger first
options.body: Keep this issue open as canonical, decide the provider-aware bucket model, then require live Codex OAuth proof before implementation lands.

options.title: Limit to wording only
options.body: Rename the residual line to a more cautious unknown-provider bucket without changing warning or compaction behavior.

options.title: Fold into broader Codex cache work
options.body: Move the diagnostics into the broader Codex thread/cache ownership work, accepting slower resolution for this visible `/context` confusion.

recommendation.title: Define the ledger first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as canonical, decide the provider-aware bucket model, then require live Codex OAuth proof before implementation lands.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the original `/context` breakdown and is the best available owner for deciding whether this should remain a core diagnostics surface or move into a narrower provider/Codex design.
